service-type.notes: Promote `service` to a declarable manifest type carrying a `transports` block (stdio|http|sse|socket). Add it to the VALID_TYPES set + the Manifest/ManifestInstall type unions, generalize the `profiles ⊆ serves` validation to `transports`, add a serviceTemplate + scaffold dispatch + `sox init service`, and a docs/guidelines/service.md contract. Do NOT remove `mcp-server` here — it stays valid; it is folded onto the service model in `mcp-as-service`. The whole-tree footgun: VALID_TYPES is duplicated in scripts/new-extension.ts — update both.

http-transport.notes: Wire the missing http transport AND the runtime dispatch the install routing implies. (1) supervisor: add `http-get` to LifecycleHealth.type + _probeHealth (http.get vs lifecycle.health.endpoint, timeout) and have it resolve the actual bound port from storePath/port.txt, polling for the file before the first probe. (2) loader.ts dispatchToAdapter: add a `service` case — the BLOCKER the install routing alone misses; without it `sox start` on a type:service throws Unknown extension type. (3) install.ts: route transport:http through the unified run-service path, and inject SOX_CONFIG_* into spec.env at the run-service registration site (registry env is currently {} — required for [inv:standard-config]). (4) host-registry: a `service` surface. Footgun: SIGTERM->stop_timeout_ms->SIGKILL must hold for a port-holder; concurrent `sox start` is a deferred non-goal ([dod.10]).

mcp-as-service.notes: Refactor mcp-server to be service[transport=stdio]: route mcp-server install/run through the SAME unified service model http-transport built, so `type:mcp-server` is mechanically sugar for a stdio-transport service. mcp-server MUST stay a valid type name (back-compat alias) and memory-server must non-regress: build/validate/install/start/health/stop + the C6 forbidden-write denial all green. This is the highest-risk state — memory-server is load-bearing (C6/A11). Footgun: do not change memory-server's extension.json; the refactor is behind the type, not in the extension.

audit-framework.notes: Verify the service primitive (service-type), the http transport + http-get health (http-transport), and mcp-server-as-service non-regression (mcp-as-service). The most likely failure: memory-server lifecycle or C6 regression after the routing refactor. Fix in source, never weaken the check.

core-engine.notes: Port scripts/tokenguard/core.py to a pure, IO-light TS library @sox/tokenguard-core: the bijective origin-tagged Mapper (token-mapping.json v2 shape), the detector pipeline (known/email/fqdn/ipv4/ipv6/mac/phone), tokenize_str/walk/request (two-pass), wire_leaks scoped to system|messages|metadata, detokenize_text (longest-first) and detokenize_sse (delta reassembly). Generalize the WOP `engagement_variants(slug,hosts)` into a neutral `identifierGroupVariants(label, members)` with no roe/engagement vocabulary. This state runs PARALLEL to the framework phase — no shared files.

core-invariants.notes: Port selftest.py + roundtrip.py invariants to Vitest: bijective+idempotent cache, reload-stable IDs, exact round-trip detokenize(tokenize(x))==x, zero-leak wire guarantee scoped to system/messages/metadata (tools untouched), SSE split-token reassembly, thinking-block passthrough, longest-first. Each is a red->green assertion. The suite IS the dod.4 proof.

audit-core.notes: Verify the core invariants all pass and that no WOP/engagement/roe vocabulary leaked into the core lib. Likely failure: a detector regex ported with a subtle anchor change breaking longest-first or boundary matching.

tg-service.notes: Scaffold tokenguard as a `service` extension (transport http) on top of @sox/tokenguard-core. Port proxy.py: port-holding HTTP server (walk port..+9, write port.txt), capture/audit policy, leak self-check, Accept-Encoding: identity. Provider-agnostic via an adapter interface; ship anthropic (SSE reassembly, thinking passthrough, request scoping) + generic (plain JSON passthrough) adapters. Config exclusively via config_schema/SOX_CONFIG_* ([ref:config-schema]); permissions enforced at the resource sink ([ref:c6-policy-guard]). The running server persists the live map continuously. Convergence point: needs BOTH framework (service+http) and core (engine) done.

tg-cli.notes: A simple CLI (invoked via `./bin/sox exec tokenguard -- <cmd>`) to seed + inspect identifiers, operating on the SAME live, continuously-persisted token map the running proxy reads. seed appends a custom entry; the running proxy reflects it without restart (file-watch or socket nudge, memoryd-style). map prints the current bijective entries. No MCP surface (out of scope by decision).

audit-service.notes: Verify the service installs/starts/health(http)/stops via the real sox CLI with zero orphans, the proxy round-trips real->token->real through a mock upstream with zero leaks, both adapters work, and a CLI-seeded id is reflected in the running proxy. Likely failure: port.txt race or the live-reload not picking up a CLI seed.

decouple-generalize.notes: Final generalization pass + the simple negative check: prove zero WOP coupling remains (no roe.json / engagement-dir / e2e-harness / wop path tokens in tokenguard-core or the tokenguard service), and document the generic, config-driven usage for any LLM API (the *_BASE_URL redirect model). This is documentation + a grep gate, not new behavior.

code-review.notes: The planner/orchestrator performs a full code review of every touched project before the final audit and records findings + resolution in code-review.md. Guard requires the review artifact present with a PASS verdict AND a clean `nx run-many -t typecheck,lint,test` across all touched projects. Reviewer gate per [dod.9].

audit-final.notes: The terminal audit: every [dod.N] proven (behavioral clauses driven through their documented entrypoint + observable asserted, with a negative control), every [ref:] conformance check, the WOP-gone negative checks, and the live demonstration harness producing the four founder-facing artifacts (agent prompts, outbound real->token diff, raw API response, inbound token->real diff). DONE is refused unless every [dod.N] emits an executed PASS.
